source.title: IBCircuit: Towards Holistic Circuit Discovery with Information Bottleneck
source.authors: Tian Bian; Yifan Niu; Chaohao Yuan; Cheng-Zhi Piao; Bing-Zhe Wu; Long-Kai Huang; Yu Rong; Ting-Yang Xu; Hong Cheng; Jia Li

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some equations and figure contents are not rendered as readable numerical data.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies a different circuit-discovery method to IOI and evaluates selected circuits against the pretrained model and against a canonical circuit. It does not replicate the original head-by-head role tests.
record.gate_note: The paper reports IOI circuit-selection and circuit-performance results. It also compares discovery methods against the canonical circuit using ROC curves. Greater-Than results and GPT-2 XL scalability results do not test the listed IOI versions: the paper does not establish that the same IOI head classes and roles occur there. Figures report threshold sweeps, but the supplied text does not provide their underlying numerical values.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. It uses IOI in GPT-2 small as a benchmark and reports only how its own IBCircuit method compares with SP, ACDC, AP and EAP. Logit difference and KL are measured on circuits each method selects, not on the IOI circuit. RQ1 does compare against the canonical circuit, but only to rank methods. It treats the canonical circuit as ground truth, and the ROC curves have no readable AUC or TPR/FPR values. So no result shows whether the canonical circuit's heads or roles are recovered, or how its faithfulness depends on evaluation choices.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that IBCircuit finds more faithful and minimal circuits than SP, ACDC, AP and EAP on IOI and Greater-Than, and that it scales to GPT-2 XL. On IOI they report better canonical-circuit recovery, and weaker logit difference than other methods only above about 90 nodes (still around 4). On Greater-Than it underperforms ACDC at low node counts.
record.recipe_differences: IBCircuit learns information gates by injecting calibrated Gaussian noise into activations, then selects components by learned weights. It differs from the original study's head ablations and patching-based tests of component roles.
record.method_sensitivity: IOI circuit metrics change across node- and edge-count thresholds. The paper also reports a trade-off between sparsity and KL Divergence as the trade-off coefficient α changes, but the supplied description of that sensitivity analysis is for IOI without reporting numeric values.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; the paper states Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025.
record.problems: The supplied text does not expose numerical values underlying the plotted threshold sweeps, and reports no uncertainty estimates. The evaluation compares IBCircuit-selected circuits and discovery methods, rather than directly testing the original head roles or criteria.
record.rows_left_out: No other IOI result rows were omitted. Greater-Than and GPT-2 XL results were left out because they do not measure the versions' stated IOI mechanisms or prompt variants.

untested.parts: The 26 heads, 7 classes, head roles, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria of the original circuit.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints and task reuse. The GPT-2 XL run is only a method-performance comparison.
Whether other methods, ablations or metrics recover essentially the same circuit. ROC curves exist, but no recoverable values or head-level overlap are reported.
Dependence of the IOI circuit's faithfulness or completeness on ablation, metric or prompt distribution.

record.verdict_notes: The record's own labels (V1/V5 limits_scope, V4 supports) are dropped. They rest on method-comparison rows about IBCircuit's circuits, and r5 has no readable ROC values. If figure data for Figure 2a were extracted, r5 could become a V4 row with real TPR/FPR values.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original 26 heads, seven head classes, their stated roles under patching, or the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria directly. It evaluates circuits found by IBCircuit on IOI.
Backup-head self-repair after ablating main name-mover heads is not tested.
The study does not test whether the same IOI head classes and roles occur in other models, sizes or checkpoints, or whether those components are reused across tasks.
Compares circuit discovery methods against a canonical circuit, but does not test different ablation types or establish that all methods recover an essentially identical circuit.
Tests circuit-size thresholds and reports Logit Difference and KL Divergence; it does not vary prompt distributions or ablation types.
Does not compare name orders, templates, or prompts with more names.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated IBCircuit-selected node circuits over different node-count thresholds on IOI.

conditions.value: node counts varied; exact values not stated in text

rows.baseline: Pretrained model output; method comparisons include SP, ACDC and AP
rows.value: The authors report higher Logit Difference with fewer nodes; above 90 nodes, IBCircuit performs less well than other methods but retains a Logit Difference around 4.
rows.note: The text describes the threshold sweep qualitatively. This evaluates the behavior of IBCircuit-selected circuits, not the original named head classes.
rows.check: This compares the study's own method with baselines: the logit difference of IBCircuit-selected node circuits across node-count sweeps. It does not measure the 26-head IOI circuit or its criteria (V1). Nor does it show how the IOI circuit's faithfulness depends on ablation, metric or prompt distribution (V5). The baseline is the other methods, not a control.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Compared KL Divergence for IBCircuit-selected node circuits at different node-count thresholds.

conditions.value: node counts varied; exact values not stated in text

rows.measure: KL Divergence between circuit and pretrained-model outputs
rows.value: The authors report lower KL Divergence at larger node counts.
rows.note: The stated trend shows a circuit-size trade-off; the supplied text gives no exact KL values for IOI.
rows.check: This is the same kind of method comparison: KL of IBCircuit node circuits against node count. It concerns the sparsity–fidelity trade-off of the authors' method, not the IOI circuit. No values can be read.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated IBCircuit-selected edge circuits over different edge-count thresholds on IOI.

conditions.value: edge counts varied; exact values not stated in text

rows.baseline: Pretrained model output; method comparisons include ACDC and EAP
rows.value: As the number of edges decreases, IBCircuit is reported to consistently achieve higher Logit Difference than ACDC and EAP.
rows.note: The result concerns IBCircuit-selected circuits and does not identify or test the original 26 heads.
rows.check: This compares edge-level IBCircuit with ACDC and EAP on logit difference across edge counts. It does not bear on the IOI circuit's composition or evaluation sensitivity. No numbers are given.

conditions.value: edge counts varied; exact values not stated in text

rows.measure: KL Divergence between circuit and pretrained-model outputs
rows.baseline: Pretrained model output; method comparisons include ACDC and EAP
rows.value: As the number of edges decreases, IBCircuit is reported to consistently achieve lower KL Divergence than ACDC and EAP.
rows.note: The text does not give exact IOI KL values for the edge-count sweep.
rows.check: This is the edge-level KL comparison of IBCircuit with ACDC and EAP, again a method comparison. No values are given.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Compared SP, ACDC, AP and IBCircuit for recovery of the canonical IOI circuit using ROC curves.
rows.measure: ROC performance for classifying nodes as canonical-circuit or non-circuit components
rows.value: The authors report that IBCircuit is competitive and notably outperforms baseline methods on IOI.
rows.note: The ROC values are plotted but not supplied numerically in the text.
rows.check: The canonical IOI circuit serves as ground truth for ranking methods. The text says IBCircuit 'notably outperforming baseline methods on the IOI task', but gives no AUC, TPR or FPR values. Agreement between methods and the canonical circuit therefore cannot be read. The state 'observed' is unsupported, and the row reports the study's own method against others.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
